updates.name: Jeffrey S. Deems
updates.bio: Center for Snow and Avalanche Studies board member who mapped Senator Beck Basin and nearby Silverton terrain in GIS in 2004, then helped with spring fieldwork. Studied snowpack variability at Montana State (MSc) and Colorado State (PhD), modeled snowmelt and climate effects on water supply as a University of Washington postdoc, then joined NSIDC and Western Water Assessment.
updates.research_interests: spatial variability of snowpack temperature; snowpack distribution and properties; snowmelt modeling; climate change effects on water supply
updates.current_title: Board of Directors member, Center for Snow and Avalanche Studies
updates.evidence: Dr. Jeffrey S. Deems has participated in CSAS affairs for some time, developing GIS of the Senator Beck Basin Study Area
updates.notes: Profile linked from the CSAS Board & Staff page (snowstudies.org/board-staff, which lists 'Jeff Deems' under Board of Directors). The profile text dates from around his 2010 addition to the board (it points to the January 2010 news item), so the NSIDC/Western Water Assessment affiliation is as of that text; the CIRES award page (cires.colorado.edu/recognition/mapping-avalanche-starting-zone-snow-depth-ground-based-lidar) lists Jeffrey Deems with NSIDC on a 2015 ground-based lidar project. Existing ORCID 0000-0002-3265-8670 checked at pub.orcid.org: name Jeffrey Deems, employment University of Colorado Boulder (consistent); kept, not re-written. cires.colorado.edu/people/jeffrey-deems and nsidc.org people URLs tried: 404. Status not written: no page states it.

updates.name: Clark Alexander
updates.bio: Director of UGA's Skidaway Institute of Oceanography and professor in geological oceanography, trained in geology and marine sedimentology (PhD, North Carolina State, 1990). Research covers continental-margin sediment processes and stratigraphy, barrier island and coastal geology, shoreline change and Quaternary sea level, coastal hazards and vulnerability, human impacts on coasts, and benthic habitat assessment.
updates.research_interests: continental-margin sediment processes; formation of stratigraphic sequences; barrier island and coastal geology; shoreline change; Quaternary sea-level history; coastal hazard and vulnerability assessment; human impacts on coasts; biological reworking of the sediment record; benthic habitat assessment
updates.current_title: Director, Skidaway Institute of Oceanography; Professor

updates.name: Alice Yeates
updates.bio: Stewardship Coordinator at Oregon's South Slough National Estuarine Research Reserve. Presented the Reserve's invasive species plan, works on its forest and upland monitoring, has given talks on the Wasson Creek stage-0 wetland-stream restoration, co-leads the NERRS upland working group and is training staff of six other reserves in South Slough's upland monitoring protocols.
updates.research_interests: invasive species planning; upland and forest monitoring; process-based (stage-0) wetland-stream restoration
updates.current_affiliation: South Slough National Estuarine Research Reserve, Oregon Department of State Lands
updates.evidence: Alice Yeates, Stewardship Coordinator, presented this plan outline and progress on the decision-making steps.
updates.notes: Source is the South Slough Reserve Management Commission packet for the 174th meeting (July 8, 2026), which includes the April 2026 minutes and the March-May 2026 stewardship report (invasive species plan, NERRS Upland Working Group co-lead, upland monitoring training for six reserves, three 2026 presentations on the Wasson Creek restoration). An ORCID record 0000-0002-0670-7467 named 'Alice Yeates' exists but carries no employment, so it was not recorded. Status not written: no page states it.
